DesignPage.title: Paper, ink, <marker>purpose</marker>.
DesignPage.description: Paper-like tool minimalism. One shared vocabulary, not one compulsory layout. Let the website have character and the workspace stay quiet.
DesignPage.examplesNotice: The existing palette and component defaults stay intact. These foundations guide product-specific adoption; the examples below use sample data, not product integrations.
DesignPage.paletteTitle: Keep the palette. Clarify the job.
DesignPage.paletteDescription: Swatches follow the current theme; hex values are the existing light-theme reference. Use semantic tokens, not these hex values in product code.
DesignPage.statusDescription: Status uses words as well as color.
DesignPage.patternsDescription: These are executable component compositions, not replacement product screens. Use the theme switcher above to inspect both themes. No product routes or behavior are changed here.
DesignPage.readingDescription: A compact list beside a comfortable reader. Select a message to change the reader; the current folder is raised paper, the selected message takes the selected tint.
DesignPage.listDescription: A continuous paper surface, aligned columns and explicit state. Use an inspector only when the workflow needs it, not to imitate Mail.
DesignPage.healthComposition: No compulsory ink shell. Health and history carry the hierarchy; semantic green, amber and red stay independent of brand yellow.
DesignPage.implementationTitle: Make it hold up in use
DesignPage.adoptTheme: Keep the existing <theme>theme</theme> and fonts. Reinstall item-list only where the new opt-in row styles are needed; its default spacing is unchanged.
DesignPage.adoptWorkspace: Put <navigation>WorkspaceNavigation</navigation> and <pane>WorkspacePane</pane> beside each other. Pane padding is local; product navigation, pane widths and scrolling remain the product’s decision.
DesignPage.adoptSelection: Use <density>density="compact"</density> for list spacing and <selected>selected</selected> for the muted row highlight. Supply the matching aria-current or aria-pressed semantics in the product.
DesignPage.adoptValidation: Validate real light / dark, narrow / wide and keyboard / touch flows before rolling out a product. This guide does not claim those integrations are done.

plan.subject: Next week's plan
plan.preview: Keep the important things in focus.
plan.body: The plan is ready. Let's start with the most important work and leave room for the details. The notes are attached to our next review; there is no need for another dashboard.

journal.subject: A quieter workspace
journal.preview: Good tools leave room for the content.
journal.body: A useful interface does not have to compete for attention. Keep navigation clear, let the reading surface breathe, and bring tools forward only when they help the task at hand.
